title: AI-guided focused ultrasound and deep learning detect aortic stenosis in novices
summary: A deep learning algorithm was developed on 6753 Mayo Clinic patients to detect moderate or greater aortic stenosis and reached AUROC 0.99 in the internal test cohort and in Arizona and Florida validation cohorts. In a prospective cohort of 1302 examinations by novice operators using AI-guided focused cardiac ultrasound, 96.6% were suitable for automated analysis, with sensitivity 93% and specificity 96%. Positive predictive value was 49.4% before expert review of AI-positive and uninterpretable examinations and 91.1% after. All sites belong to one health system.
ai_technology: Deep learning algorithm for aortic stenosis detection plus AI-guided focused cardiac ultrasound acquisition

evidence.tested: Retrospective development and validation (n=6753 development; 1912 validation) and prospective novice-operator acquisition (n=1302) against echocardiographic reference.
evidence.unknown: Single health system (Mayo Clinic sites); PPV 49.4% before expert review; clinical outcomes and cost-effectiveness not assessed; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning model reads focused cardiac ultrasound to flag moderate or greater aortic stenosis and guides acquisition.
